definition: Training a model on a large, unlabeled corpus with a self-supervised objective before task-specific adaptation.
details: Pre-training learns general representations from abundant raw data — predicting the next word, filling masked tokens, or matching context. ELMo demonstrated that deeply contextualized word representations from a pre-trained language model improved many NLP tasks, setting the pattern of pre-train-then-adapt that all modern LLMs follow.

explainer.lead: Pre-training is the first, large-scale stage that gives a model general language ability before any task-specific tuning. It matters because this pre-train-then-adapt pattern underlies all modern LLMs.

tiers.eli5: It's like reading a huge library of books before starting a job, so you already know a lot before anyone trains you on the specific task.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers pre-train on a large unlabeled corpus with a self-supervised objective, then adapt the resulting representations to downstream tasks. A pitfall is treating pre-training as task-ready: it learns general representations, not the target task, so adaptation is still required.
tiers.paperLevel: Train on a large unlabeled corpus with a self-supervised objective such as next-word prediction, masked-token filling, or context matching, producing general representations; the method is only as broad as the raw data and objective allow.

explainer.example: ELMo pre-trained a language model to produce deeply contextualized word representations, which then improved many NLP tasks.
